title: In re Pers. Restraint of Cross v. State
questions: Can a defendant facing a death penalty plead "no contest"?

title: McDevitt v. Harborview Medical Center
questions: Whether the medical malpractice claim notice requirements of RCW 7.70.100(1), found unconstitutional in Waples v. Yi, 169 Wn.2d 152, 234 P.3d 187 (2010), remain applicable to malpractice suits against the State.

title: In re Thomas R. Kamb, Attorney at Law
questions: The Court must determine whether attorney Thomas R. Kamb violated the Rules of Professional Conduct and impose appropriate sanctions for any violations.

title: In re Rosaura Del Carmen Rodriguez, Attorney at Law
questions: The Court will decide whether the evidence supports a finding that attorney Rosaura Del Carmen Rodriguez violated the Rules of Professional Conduct and impose an appropriate sanction.

title: Tan & Vietnamese Cmty. of Thurston County v. Le
questions: Whether statements accusing a Vietnamese immigrant and public figure of being a communist and an agent of the government of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam were defamatory assertions of purported fact, and if so, whether they were made with actual malice.

title: State of Washington v. Coristine
questions: Whether, in a prosecution for second degree rape by means of intercourse with a person unable to consent due to mental incapacity or physical helplessness, the trial court properly instructed the jury on the affirmative defense of reasonable belief that the victim was capable of consent, even though the defendant objected to the instruction and asserted only the defense that the State could not prove that the victim was incapacitated.

title: State of Washington v. Ortega
questions: Whether the defendant in a misdemeanor drug prosecution was lawfully arrested when the officer who witnessed the crime did not make the arrest but directed other officers who did not witness the crime to make the arrest.

title: In re Custody of A.F.J.
questions: Whether a foster parent who is also the former intimate partner of the child’s biological mother may seek the status of a de facto parent.

title: In re the Custody of A.F.J.
questions: The court must decide if service as a foster parent alone precludes a finding of de facto parentage.

title: National Surety Corp. v. Immunex Corp.
questions: Whether an insurer may be required to reimburse its insured for defense expenditures incurred from the date that a complaint was filed against the insured until entry of a declaratory judgment that the insurer had no duty to defend the suit.

title: State of Washington v. Saintcalle
questions: Whether the trial court in a criminal prosecution erred in allowing the State to use a peremptory challenge to exclude the only African-American potential juror after she expressed concern about the fairness of the criminal justice system toward young African-American men.

title: Cornu-Labat v. Hospital District No. 2 Grant County
questions: Whether records of a public hospital's investigation of a staff physician are exempt from public disclosure as privileged peer review committee records under RCW 4.24.250, privileged quality improvement committee records under RCW 70.41.200, or confidential public hospital district commission deliberations concerning a physician's medical staff privileges under RCW 70.44.062(1).

title: State of Washington v. Byrd
questions: Whether the warrantless search of a car occupant's purse incident to the occupant's arrest outside the car is unlawful under Arizona v. Gant, 556 U.S. 332, 129 S. Ct. 1710, 173 L. Ed. 2d 435 (2009).

title: State of Washington v. Ruem
questions: Whether police officers seeking consent to enter a defendant's home to execute an arrest warrant on the defendant's brother were required to advise the defendant of his right to refuse consent under State v. Ferrier, 136 Wn.2d 262, 960 P.2d 927 (1998).

title: Lowman v. Puget Sound Energy
questions: Whether in this personal injury action a utility company's approved placement of a utility pole closer to a roadway than allowed by county regulations constituted a legal cause of damages the plaintiff suffered when the car he was riding in struck the pole while being driven recklessly.

title: In re Estate of James W. Haviland
questions: Whether an amendment to the slayer statute, RCW 11.84.020, extending the statute to abusers is given improper retroactive effect when applied to a petition to adjudicate as an abuser a beneficiary of a decedent who died before the effective date of the amendment.

title: Clark County Washington v. Western Washington Growth Management Hearings Review Board
questions: Did the Growth Management Hearings Review Board's review of Clark County's designation of certain lands as UGA become moot when those lands were annexed?

title: Schroeder v. Excelsior Management Group
questions: Under WA's Deed of Trust Act, is agricultural land subject to nonjudicial foreclosure?

title: State of Washington v. Veliz
questions: Whether a domestic violence protection order entered in connection with a marriage dissolution proceeding was a “court-ordered parenting plan,” violation of which constituted the crime of first degree custodial interference under RCW 9A.40.060(2).

title: State of Washington v. Ollivier
questions: Whether in this criminal prosecution a 22-month delay between the filing of the charge and the start of trial violated the defendant's constitutional right to a speedy trial.

title: State of Washington v. Evans
questions: Whether a corporation is a "person" that can be a victim of identity theft.

title: Donatelli v. D.R. Strong Consulting Eng'rs, Inc.
questions: Whether in an action arising out of a contract for engineering services the independent duty doctrine permits the client's tort claims against the engineering firm for negligence and negligent misrepresentation.

title: State of Washington v. Duncalf
questions: Whether in light of Blakely v. Washington, 542 U.S. 296, 124 S. Ct. 2531, 159 L. Ed. 2d 403 (2004), sentence aggravating factors may be challenged as unconstitutionally vague, and if so, whether the factor based on the infliction of bodily harm that "substantially exceeds" the level necessary to satisfy the elements of the crime is unconstitutionally vague.

title: State of Washington v. Meredith
questions: Whether in a criminal prosecution of a Caucasian defendant the trial court erred in allowing the State to use a peremptory challenge to exclude the sole African-American potential juror from the jury panel.

title: Piel v. City of Federal Way
questions: Whether a public employee who claims he was terminated for engaging in union organizing activity may maintain a tort action for wrongful termination in violation of public policy on the basis of the policy expressed in the Public Employees' Collective Bargaining Act, chapter 41.56 RCW.

title: Dep’t of Ecology v. Acquavella
questions: Whether the trial court properly determined the existence, scope, and priority of Yakama Indian Nation and non-Indian parties’ water rights in the Ahtanum Creek sub-basin of the Yakima River Basin.

title: Freedom Foundation v. Gregoire
questions: Does the Washington State Constitution provide the governor with an executive privilege that allows her to withhold documents requested under Washington's Public Records Act?

title: City of Seattle v. Fuller
questions: Whether the Seattle Municipal Court, in ordering a partially suspended sentence for a state crime, had authority to impose both a fine and restitution.

title: In re Personal Restraint Petition of Finstad
questions: Whether a judgment and sentence based on a plea of guilty is facially invalid, and thus subject to collateral attack more than one year after the judgment became final, because it imposed consecutive standard range sentences on nonviolent offenses without findings on aggravating circumstances and without a stipulation by the petitioner to an exceptional sentence, and if so, whether the petitioner is entitled to be resentenced.

title: League of Education Voters v. State
questions: Whether plaintiffs challenging the constitutionality of RCW 43.135.034, which requires supermajority legislative approval of tax increases and voter approval of tax increases that result in spending above the state limit, have standing and present a justiciable controversy, and if so, whether the statute conflicts with state constitutional provisions governing referenda and requiring a simple majority to pass most legislative measures.

title: State of Washington v. Smith
questions: Whether evidence of crimes discovered as a result of an inquiry that began with an unlawful search of a motel registry was derived from an independent source or was attenuated from the unlawful search, so as to allow the evidence to be admitted to trial.

title: In re Custody of B.M.H.
questions: Whether a former stepparent may acquire the status of defacto parent of a child with only one living biological parent, and whether the former stepparent in this case made an adequate showing that relocation of the child to a different city would be detrimental to the child's growth and development, justifying a

title: State of Washington v. Tyler
questions: Whether consent is required to conduct an inventory search of a vehicle prior to impoundment, and if not, whether the purported inventory search here was a pretext for a search for evidence otherwise unlawful under Arizona v. Gant, 556 U.S. 332, 129 S. Ct. 1710, 173 L. Ed. 2d 485 (2009).

title: Barton v. State Department of Transportation
questions: Whether two defendants in a negligence action remained jointly and severally liable after one of the defendants entered into an undisclosed pretrial agreement with the plaintiff limiting that defendant's liability should the plaintiff prevail at trial.

title: State of Washington v. Jorgenson
questions: Whether RCW 9.41.040(2)(a)(iv) is unconstitutional in criminalizing the possession of firearms by a person charged with a serious offense and free on bond or personal recognizance pending trial.

title: State of Washington v. Siegel
questions: Whether the superior court erred in denying a motion to unseal records of a vacated criminal conviction without making findings required by GR 15 or Seattle Times Co. v. Ishikawa, 97 Wn.2d 30, 640 P.2d 716 (1982).

title: Klem v. Washington Mutual Bank
questions: Whether the trustee in a nonjudicial foreclosure violated the Consumer Protection Act by deferring to the lender on whether to grant the debtor's request to postpone the foreclosure sale, and by predating the notarized notice of sale.

title: State of Washington v. Kurtz
questions: Whether a person who lacks authority to possess or manufacture marijuana under the Medical Use of Marijuana Act, chapter 69.51A RCW, may assert a common law medical necessity defense in a prosecution for unlawful manufacture and possession of marijuana.

title: Skagit County Public Hospital District No. 304 v. Skagit County Public Hospital District No. 1
questions: Whether a public hospital district may operate a medical clinic within another district's territorial boundaries without the other district's permission.

title: Lakey v. Puget Sound Energy
questions: Whether residential neighbors of a new Puget Sound Energy substation may bring an inverse condemnation action against the city of Kirkland to recover compensation for reduced property values without having challenged the city’s approval of the substation by land use petition, and whether the neighbors presented valid scientific evidence of the adverse health effects of electromagnetic fields enabling their nuisance suit against Puget Sound Energy to proceed.

title: Resident Action Council v. Seattle Housing Authority
questions: Whether the Seattle Housing Authority violated the Public Records Act when it disclosed previously redacted copies of public housing assistance tenant grievance decisions, and if so, whether the trial court properly ordered the Authority to create new records with fewer redactions, to provide them in electronic format, and to promulgate procedures relating to such record requests.

title: Condon v. Condon
questions: Whether, after the parties to a personal injury suit entered into a settlement agreement and stipulated to dismissal of the action, the trial court had authority under CR 2A to enforce the settlement and deem a release of claims to have been signed by the plaintiff.

title: Chicago Title Insurance v. Office of the Insurance Commissioner
questions: Whether a statewide title insurance company that underwrote policies for a local title insurance company may be held vicariously liable for the local company's violations of insurance regulations.

title: Swinomish Indian Tribal Community v. Washington State Department of Ecology
questions: Whether the Department of Ecology exceeded its authority and acted arbitrarily and capriciously in amending the Skagit River Instream Flow Rule to authorize new appropriations of water from Skagit River tributary subbasins for domestic, commercial, municipal, and agricultural uses.

title: Lemire v. State
questions: Whether RCW 90.48.120, which authorizes the Department of Ecology to order corrective action against the discharge of pollutants into state waters, allowed the department to issue an order regulating cattle grazing on ranch land so as to prevent pollution of a creek, and if so, whether the order in this case constituted a taking of property for public use entitling the landowner to compensation.

title: Ameriquest Mortgage Company v. Washington State Office of the Attorney General
questions: Whether in relation to a public disclosure request for records supplied to the Washington attorney general by a mortgage company in an investigation of its lending practices, the attorney general is prohibited by the federal Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act from releasing emails generated by company employees during the processing of consumer loans, whether the materials are exempt from disclosure under the Public Records Act as investigative records, and whether the Consumer Protection Act prohibits disclosure of the records because they are the result of a civil investigative demand.

title: Sargent v. Seattle Police Department
questions: Whether the exemption from the Public Records Act for law enforcement investigative records expired when the underlying case was referred for prosecution, and if so, whether the law enforcement agency was thereafter required to comply with the original public records request.

title: State of Washington v. Clark
questions: Whether nontribal police officers were required to obtain a search warrant from a tribal court in order to search the home of a tribal member located on tribal land for evidence of a crime committed on fee land within the boundaries of an Indian reservation.

title: King County v. King County
questions: Whether a materials processing facility was a valid nonconforming use even though it was established in part by nonpermitted clearing and grading.

title: Cedar River Water & Sewer District v. King County
questions: Whether Snohomish County’s approval of community mitigation projects related to a sewage treatment facility was a land use decision subject to the time limit on judicial challenges under the Land Use Petition Act.

title: Columbia Community Bank v. Newman Park
questions: Whether a subsequent “volunteer” lender foreclosing on a deed of trust may be equitably subrogated to a previous loan encumbering the real property.

title: Raven v. Department of Social & Health Services
questions: Whether in an action for neglect of a ward under the abuse of vulnerable adults act, chapter 74.34 RCW, the State need only prove the guardian engaged in a pattern of conduct resulting in a deprivation of care, not that the conduct caused the ward harm or that the ward would have accepted an alternative care plan had one been offered.

title: In re the Estate of Virgil Becker
questions: Whether the spouse of a decedent, who is not a beneficiary under the will, had standing to intervene in a will contest in order to challenge a settlement between the will challengers and the guardian ad litem of the surviving spouse’s minor child, the sole beneficiary under the will.

title: Kofmehl v. Baseline Lake
questions: Whether a seller who claims to be ready, willing, and able to perform a real estate sales contract that violates the statute of frauds may avoid the remedy of restitution of the earnest money if the parties disagree as to the terms of the contract, and if so, whether the buyer bears the burden of proving that the seller is not ready, willing, and able to perform.

title: Stewart Title Guaranty v. Sterling Savings Bank
questions: Whether equitable subrogation was available to a bank on the basis of a construction and purchase loan to a developer intended to pay off existing liens on the property, giving the bank priority over a subsequent mechanic’s lien.

title: Dean v. Fishing Company of Alaska
questions: Whether in a Jones Act case brought by a maritime worker the trial court correctly applied the summary judgment standard to the worker’s pretrial motion to reinstate maintenance and cure.

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Haghighi
questions: The trial court admitted evidence at Mr. Haghighi's trial under the inevitable discovery doctrine. After Mr. Haghighi's judgment was final, this court rejected the use of the inevitable discovery doctrine in another case. This court must decide whether that case applies retroactively to Mr. Haghighi's judgment.

title: International Marine Underwriters v. ABCD Marine, LLC
questions: Synopsis: Whether a partner in a general partnership qualifies as a third party to an indemnification agreement between the partnership and another business bringing the personal injuries he suffered while on the job within the coverage provided by the partnership's comprehensive general liability insurance policy.

title: Freeman v. State of Washington
questions: Does the State's lease of a portion of I-90 to Sound Transit violate article II, section 40 of the Washington Constitution and RCW 47.12.120?

title: In re Starczewski, Attorney at Law
questions: Was Starczewski's disciplinary hearing fair and proper, and should the Disciplinary Board’s penalties be affirmed?

title: State of Washington v. Sanchez
questions: Whether, in light of a 2011 amendment to RCW 7.09.345 that requires the end-of-sentence review committee to assign risk levels to sex offenders (Laws of 2011, ch. 338, Â§ 5), a juvenile court was nonetheless required by RCW 4.24.550(6) to transmit a juvenile offender’s Special Sex Offender Disposition Alternative evaluation to the county sheriff for risk classification.

title: In re Wickersham, Attorney at Law
questions: The court reviews findings of misconduct against an attorney and decides whether to impose a three-year suspension.

title: Brown v. MHN Government Services, Inc.
questions: Whether a mandatory arbitration clause in a contract between social service professionals and a corporation that provides social and counseling services to members of the military is unconscionable.

title: Jafar v. Webb
questions: Whether a superior court, upon finding a litigant indigent in connection with an application to waive filing fees and surcharges under General Rule 34, must waive all fees and surcharges or may grant a partial waiver.

title: State of Washington v. Vasquez
questions: Whether a defendant’s possession of forged documents without evidence that the defendant used the documents for any purpose supports an inference of intent to defraud sufficient to convict the defendant of forgery.

title: King County Public Hospital No. 2 v. Washington State Department of Health
questions: Whether the Department of Health properly issued a certificate of need in settlement of an adjudicative hearing on the validity of the department’s original decision denying a certificate, and whether in doing so it properly relied on data collected after the original decision.

title: In re Sanai, Attorney at Law
questions: Sanai was disbarred following a disciplinary process; did this process violate Sanai's constitutional rights?

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Lain
questions: Whether the governor’s power under RCW 9.95.160 to “cancel or revoke” an offender’s probation authorizes the governor to overrule a decision of the Indeterminate Sentence Review Board granting probation, and if so, whether the offender is entitled to due process protections.

title: State of Washington v. Lynch
questions: In a second degree rape case, did the trial court violate Lynch's constitutional rights when it instructed the jury that Lynch had the burden of proving consent?

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Adams
questions: A trial court sentenced Devon Adams in 2000 for first degree murder and unlawful possession of a firearm. Adams claims that because he was re-sentenced in 2009, he should now be able to raise an ineffectiveness of trial counsel claim

title: State of Washington v. McEnroe
questions: Whether the State violates Washington statutes and a defendant's rights to equal protection under the law when, in deciding whether to file a notice to seek the death penalty, the State considers the strength of the evidence of the defendant's guilt in addition to the sufficiency of any mitigating circumstances

title: State of Washington v. Mau
questions: A jury found that the petitioner presented false information to the claims adjuster for a self-insured rental truck company. In doing so, did she commit the crime of presenting a false claim "for payment of a loss under a contract of insurance?"

title: State of Washington v. Chen
questions: Whether the trial court erred in refusing to seal the defendant's competency evaluation in light of RCW 10.77.210, which limits disclosure of competency evaluations.

title: NANETTE AURDAL, et ux v. UNITED TELEPHONE COMPANY OF THE NORTHWEST, dba SPRINT
questions: Can Burnston argue on appeal that the hit-and-run statute does not apply to collisions with a horse? Does it?

title: State of Washington v. Dye
questions: Does it violate a defendant's fair trial rights for the developmentally disabled victim to have a facility dog present during his testimony

title: Cost Mgmt. Servs. v. City of Lakewood
questions: Cost Management Services (CMS) asked the City of Lakewood for a refund of taxes. Lakewood issued a demand to CMS for payment of taxes that did not mention the refund request. Was CMS required to exhaust its administrative remedies in Lakewood before bringing a case in state court for its refund claim?

title: State of Washington v. Wooten
questions: Can a defendant be convicted of malicious mischief for damaging a house he was purchasing on a real estate contract?

title: Hill v. Garda CL Nw. Inc.
questions: The court considers issues stemming from a trial court's order to compel class arbitration in a labor dispute.

title: Frizzell v. Murray
questions: Whether the grantor of a deed of trust waived her right to assert post sale challenges following a trustee's non-judicial foreclosure sale when she failed to enjoin the sale

title: State of Washington v. Zillyette
questions: Is an information charging a defendant with controlled substances homicide valid when it fails to specify what drug killed the victim?

title: State of Washington v. Bao Dinh Dang
questions: Must a trial court find persons acquitted by reason of insanity dangerous before revoking their conditional release from commitment, and, if so, under what standard of proof? In addition, was the trial court's admission of hearsay evidence at the hearing to revoke Dang's conditional release reversible error?

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against McGrath
questions: The court reviews findings of misconduct against an attorney and decides whether to disbar him

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Brockie
questions: Benjamin Brockie challenges his robbery and kidnapping convictions because the jury was instructed on a means of committing robbery that was not described in the charges against him.

title: In Re Marriage of Buecking
questions: Does the 90 day waiting period for a dissolution decree begin with the filing of a petition for legal separation and, if not, does a court have jurisdiction to enter a decree before 90 days have elapsed?

title: Jones v. City of Seattle
questions: A jury awarded the plaintiff $12.75 million for injuries that her brother, Mark, sustained as a result of the City's negligence. The City seeks a new trial on damages, arguing that it has surveillance video proving that Mark is not as injured as he claimed to be. Did the trial judge abuse her discretion when she excluded three of the City's witnesses because they were disclosed after trial had already started, or when she denied the City's motion for a new trial because she found it had not exercised "reasonable diligence" in investigating Mark's physical condition?

title: Washburn v. City of Federal Way
questions: Can the court consider the City of Federal Way's arguments that it is not liable for the death of Baerbel K. Roznowski? If so, is the City liable?

title: In re Parentage of C.M.F.
questions: Whether a parentage order is a custody decree that a court cannot change without following the statutory requirements, found in RCW 26.09.260 and .270, for modification.

title: Friends of Columbia Gorge, Inc. v. State Energy Facility Site Evaluation Council
questions: Whether the Energy Facility Site Evaluation Council and Governor properly granted approval for the Whistling Ridge Wind Energy Project?

title: State of Washington v. Monfort
questions: May a county prosecutor consider the facts of the crime when determining whether to seek the death penalty? And, did the county prosecutor in this case consider sufficient mitigating circumstances when determining whether to seek the death penalty?

title: Washington Education Association, Et Al. v. Washington Department of Retirement Systems
questions: The Uniform Cost of Living Adjustment (UCOLA) added an extra sum onto each state retiree's monthly pension payment to account for changes in cost of living and increased inflation. This court considers whether the repeal provisions of UCOLA unconstitutionally impaired the state's contract with its employees.

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Yates
In re Pers. Restraint of Netherton
Weidert v. Producers Agric. Ins. Co.

In Re Pers. Restraint of Gronquist
